LLM agents, cloud systems and browser-native tools. Most of the Projects page comes from here.
Financial systems and market data — the origin of Traddy, a portfolio and trading interface for Interactive Brokers.
Industrial and energy systems, where a model being wrong has physical consequences rather than merely inconvenient ones.
The first discipline, and the reason I tend to want a model I can take apart and check rather than one I have to take on faith.

rules.name: Do the work once
rules.blurb: Quickmini trims and compresses in a single ffmpeg pass. Two passes would decode and re-encode the video twice and lose quality to a second round of compression, for no gain. Most speed comes from removing a step, not tuning one.

rules.name: Silently wrong beats slow — never
rules.blurb: Stream copy made trims about 20× faster, but cuts can only land on keyframes: a requested 7.0s trim exported 18.8s with no error. It was removed. An output that is quietly incorrect costs far more than one that takes 25 seconds.

rules.name: Write down what didn't work
rules.blurb: The multithreaded ffmpeg core deadlocks mid-encode; VP9 crashes the wasm heap where VP8 survives. Both are recorded in the source with what was observed, so nobody — including me — spends another afternoon rediscovering them.

rules.name: Prove it against the real thing
rules.blurb: A page that loads proves nothing. Quickmini's export was 100% broken while the interface looked perfect, because the failure only appeared once Export was actually clicked. Verification happens against the deployed site, not localhost.
